newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Violence heats up at Israel-Lebanon border.
newsitem.headline: Violence heats up at Israel-Lebanon border.

text.p: Violence escalated on Thursday at the Israel-Lebanon border where Israel Radio said at least one pro-Israeli fighter and an Arab guerrilla were killed.
Mortar rounds fired from Lebanon exploded at Israel's northern border, injuring no one, military sources said. The army said earlier its warplanes struck a guerrilla target in southern Lebanon.

Israeli military sources confirmed a pro-Israeli South Lebanon Army militiaman was killed and three were lightly wounded when a roadside bomb exploded late on Wednesday in the Jezzine area just outside Israel's south Lebanon occupation zone.

In Beirut, the pro-Iranian Hizbollah (Party of God) claimed responsibility. SLA sources said the explosion prompted retaliatory Israeli shelling north of Jezzine. Israel Radio said one guerrilla was killed in fighting overnight.

Israeli warplanes attacked guerrilla targets overnight in the eastern sector of the security zone, reported accurate hits and returned safely to base, an army spokeswoman said. The mortar rounds exploded at the border around dawn on Thursday.

The 3,000-strong SLA militia helps some 1,000 Israeli troops hold a 15-km (nine-mile)-deep zone in south Lebanon to guard northern Israel from guerrilla attacks. Hizbollah targets Israeli and SLA fighters in a bid to drive the Israelis from the occupation zone.
